subject: Incident synthesis & QBR action commitments
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Incident synthesis: high-latency window (2026-10-11) and proposed QBR commitments

Team,

TL;DR: The 10/11 high-latency event caused 4 hours of degraded tail latency for hosted API customers, primarily affecting the small-size routing cluster in us-west-2. Root cause currently narrowed to an autoscaling race condition that left a generation of workers with inconsistent KV cache warmup. Impact: ~2.1% of total token throughput in that window; three paying accounts (including CoreFin) reported observable P95 latency spikes and one requested an incident credit.

Attached: incident_postmortem_draft.pdf (working draft) and a short action register. I summarized the key ask areas below with proposed owners. Please review and confirm owner/ETA so I can fold into the QBR packet by EOD Tues.

Impact summary
- Window: 2026-10-11T02:16–06:20 UTC
- Impact: 4 hrs degraded tail latency; P95 up to 1.6s from baseline 0.28s for certain request shapes
- Customers affected (identified): CoreFin (prod), ProcureOps (staging), and one self-hosted partner who routed through our dedicated pool

Proposed QBR action commitments (short):
1) Engineering: fix autoscaler race + KV warmup lock (owner: Marcus Lin) — target: patch + canary by 10/25
2) Platform/Infra: introduce a conservative autoscale fallback policy for small pools, enable extra warmup steps (owner: Marissa Cole) — target: 11/05
3) Customer Success/Eng: reach out to CoreFin + ProcureOps with tailored remediation and credit proposal (owner: Vivek Kulkarni) — target: initial outreach by 10/19
4) Ops: add monitoring alert for mismatched KV states across worker generations (owner: Hannah Schmitt) — target: 10/22

Attachments: incident_postmortem_draft.pdf (notes, timeline, initial RCA), qbr_action_register_v1.xlsx (owner table).

Next steps: I will update the postmortem with Marcus' final technical notes and the canary plan. Please flag any timeline conflicts.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

---

Marcus — thanks for the clear distillation. A few leadership notes:

1) For the QBR exec packet I want a one-page customer-impact summary that lists: customers affected, minutes of degraded SLAs per customer, proposed remediation/credit (range), and a single-line owner/ETA. Keep it consumable for the CRO/CFO.
2) OKR alignment: please map the engineering fix to Reliability OKR R1 (Reduce P95 tail variance) and include the expected metric delta if we implement your patch + warmup.
3) Risk to QBR narrative: we own the first half of the story (root cause + fix), but we need Customer Success outreach documented and a draft credit proposal before we present. Vivek — can you own the customer comms and give me a draft by 10/19 noon PT?

Also: include a short line on whether this should change our SLA wording or escalation matrix. My sense: operational change only, no SLA rewrite required unless legal flags the credit impact.

Please include the condensed one-pager as exec_one_pager.docx in the folder. Marcus/Marissa — confirm owners and realistic ETAs by COB today so I can lock slides.

Date: 2026-10-18T17:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident synthesis: high-latency window (2026-10-11) and proposed QBR commitments

Evelyn / team — I can take point on customer comms and the credit proposal. Quick items:

- Outreach plan: send a personalized incident summary + proposed credit band (2–5% of the monthly invoice for affected window) to CoreFin and ProcureOps by 10/19 EOD. If CoreFin pushes back we will escalate to legal.
- Exec ask: please confirm whether the leadership packet should include a request for a one-time discretionary credit approval up to $25k for CoreFin (if they request). If leadership pre-approves a credit band it speeds CS responses.
- QBR slot: we should reserve a 5–7 minute slot for the incident narrative and remedial commitments and mark the slide as "Operational risk mitigated; monitoring in place."

Marcus: can you confirm whether the canary by 10/25 will include a rollback plan and the test harness for warmup validation? If yes, I'll include that in the outreach to the customers (they often want to know how we validate).

I'll draft comms and put the email copy + credit calc in the Drive folder and share the DocuSign/approval link if needed.

Vivek
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
